system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Green Bancorp, Inc. realized record after the 2019 acquisition, ~3-5-year horizon

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The acquired company deregistered after the
> transaction and filed no further periodic reports; where a realized record might
> otherwise be observable it is traced through the acquirer's subsequent Form 10-K, which
> itself states the acquirer does not separately report the acquired business. This
> sub-dossier contains no information about how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status of the acquired entity after the transaction
- Green Bancorp, Inc.'s last annual report as an independent registrant was its Form 10-K
  for fiscal year 2017, filed 2018-03-15; no Form 10-K covering fiscal year 2018 or any
  later period was filed under Green's registrant CIK. [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-18-003234, Form 10-K]
- The merger completed January 1, 2019; Green notified the Nasdaq Global Select Market
  that, effective as of that date, Green common stock would be converted into the right to
  receive merger consideration, and Nasdaq filed a Form 25-NSE on 2018-12-31 reporting the
  removal of Green common stock from listing. [SRC: SEC accession 0001501570-19-000005, Form 8-K Item 3.01; SEC accession 0001354457-18-000552, Form 25-NSE]
- Green (by then represented by Veritex "as successor to Green Bancorp, Inc.") filed a
  Form 15-12B on 2019-01-10 certifying termination of registration of its common stock,
  stating that as of that date there were no holders of record of Green common stock. [SRC: SEC accession 0001606363-19-000009, Form 15-12B]
- Consequently, no separate audited public financial statements exist for Green Bancorp,
  Inc. for the fixed ~3–5-year (approximately 2021–2023) outcome window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001606363-19-000009, Form 15-12B]

## Extent to which the acquirer separately discloses the acquired business
- Veritex Holdings, Inc. (the surviving corporation, CIK 1501570) continued as an SEC
  reporting company after the merger. [SRC: SEC accession 0001501570-22-000039, Form 10-K]
- In its Form 10-K for fiscal year 2021 (filed 2022-03-01), Veritex states that "Our
  business is conducted through one reportable segment, community banking," and, in its
  segment-reporting footnote, that "The Company has one reportable segment. All of the
  Company's activities are interrelated, and each activity is dependent and assessed based
  on how each activity of the Company supports the others." [SRC: SEC accession 0001501570-22-000039, Form 10-K]
- The same Form 10-K lists "Green Bank ('Green') through Green Bancorp, Inc." among a
  table of prior bank acquisitions (acquired January 2019, 21 branches, Houston and
  Dallas) as historical background; it does not present a separate segment, business
  line, or line-item financial disclosure for the former Green Bank business distinct from
  Veritex's consolidated, single-segment results. [SRC: SEC accession 0001501570-22-000039, Form 10-K]

## Items noted but not primary-verifiable within the fixed window
- General web search located only pre-closing, forward-looking integration-risk language
  (e.g., risk-factor boilerplate about integration, cost synergies, and customer/employee
  disruption) rather than any documented post-closing integration outcome specific to the
  former Green business; no such documented outcome was retrieved from a primary source. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Green Bancorp, Inc. deregistered its common stock (Form 25-NSE, 2018-12-31; Form
  15-12B, 2019-01-10) following the merger's completion and filed no further periodic
  reports, so no standalone audited trajectory exists for it in the fixed ~2021–2023
  outcome window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001354457-18-000552, Form 25-NSE] [SRC: SEC accession 0001606363-19-000009, Form 15-12B] The acquirer, Veritex Holdings,
  Inc., remained a reporting company but its Form 10-K for fiscal year 2021 explicitly
  states it operates through a single reportable segment with interrelated activities, and
  presents no segment, business-line, or line-item disclosure that separately isolates the
  former Green Bank business's post-acquisition financial trajectory. [SRC: SEC accession 0001501570-22-000039, Form 10-K] Because no
  separate public record of the acquired business's realized trajectory exists — and per
  the no-record rule, none is inferred from Veritex's undifferentiated consolidated
  results — the outcome over the fixed window is coded uncertain rather than fabricated or
  inferred. [SRC: SEC accession 0001501570-22-000039, Form 10-K]

[SLICE END]
